11.2 TrueAllele World
Typically, a new TrueAllele World is created when a case is received. Multiple cases
can also be solved on the same TrueAllele World. This section contains guidelines for
annotating and creating a TrueAllele World for a case using the VUIer software.




Create World

  TrueAllele® Casework SOP       Cybergenetics Ó 2024                   Page 71 of 116




                                          003766
Using the Tools module, the obtainer, planner, or operator creates a TrueAllele World.
The date the case is received is generally included in the World Information window
(TrueAllele World > Information).


Add Client
A client name is added to the World. This name is typically a shortened acronym of the
client’s office name (e.g., Allegheny County District Attorney’s Office client name is
ACDA). Any name can be used, however. Contact information can be added, if known.
These additional fields can be left blank.


Add Lab
A lab name is added to the World. This name is typically a shortened acronym of the
lab’s name (e.g., Pennsylvania State Police lab name is PSP). Any name can be used,
however. Contact information can be added, if known. These additional fields can be
left blank.



11.3 Request Naming
Overview
When creating a request, the planner or operator may name a request using the fields
in the listed order. This order standardizes the request name regardless of which fields
are used. Note that each field is separated by the underscore ‘_’ symbol in the request
name. This standardized naming allows features like the Match Screening Table to
group requests.


Case name
The case name can be used when multiple cases are on the same World. If the World
contains only one case, the case name can be omitted from the request name.


Item name

  TrueAllele® Casework SOP          Cybergenetics Ó 2024                 Page 72 of 116




                                             003767
The item name may or may not be the sample/lane/exhibit name. Typically, the VUIer
DNA item name and the Request item name are identical.


Optional item name fields are available and follow the item name in the indicated order:


- lab name
- kit name
- well number
- amplification number
- injections number


If multiple items are joined in a request (whether known reference or other evidence),
the planner/operator can separate each item with the plus sign ‘+’ symbol. Try to avoid
using the underscore “_” separator character within item names.


For some older cases, data processed above 0 rfu may be indicated by having the peak
height level added to the request name (e.g., 5rfu). This field follows the item name and
is usually separated by an underscore.


For cases where only some of the evidence data is rescaled, add “_rsc” after the item
name (e.g., Q1_rsc) to indicate that the 3500 rescale feature was used for this item.


Number of contributors
When creating the request, the planner or operator indicates the total number of
contributors assumed to be present in the evidence using the following field where # is
replaced with the actual numeric value.


- ncon#


Options

  TrueAllele® Casework SOP       Cybergenetics Ó 2024                  Page 73 of 116




                                          003768
When an option is used, such as the degraded DNA feature, the option may be
indicated using the code below:

 Option                           Code
 Off ladder - Medium              OL2
 Off ladder - Large               OL3
 Differentially degraded mixture dgrd
 Sort contributors                sort


Number of cycles
The planner/operator may indicate the cycling parameters where the # character is
replaced by the numeric value(s) for the thousands of cycles used.

- #K


Request naming example
Case LB2011 has three evidence items 1A, 2B, and 3C. Items 1A and 2B contain 2
total contributors. As item 1A is an intimate sample, the reference K1 can be used in
the genotype inference. Item 2B is amped twice in wells A12 and H09. The number of
contributors in item 3C may be two or three, and this item was analyzed using the 3500
rescale feature. Each request was processed with a cycle time of 50,000/50,000. The
example case naming is shown in the table below.


Request name                         Description

LB2011_1A+K1_ncon2_50K               Item 1A with reference K1 as a known contributor

LB2011_2B_A12_ncon2_50K              Item 2B in well A12

LB2011_2B_H09_ncon2_50K              Item 2B in well H09

LB2011_3C_rsc_ncon3_50K              Item 3C, rescaled, assuming three total contributors




  TrueAllele® Casework SOP        Cybergenetics Ó 2024                 Page 74 of 116

Request timing
-    Use the first database query to gather the start date, the finish date, and duration
     times for the requests:
     •   Open a terminal window.
     •   Connect to the server.
     •   Login to the case World: psql <worldname>.
     •   Enter the password at the prompt.
     •   Enter the database query below.
         o Replace the dash, quotes, and/or commas as needed for the command to
            work properly.


select name, date(started) as started, date(finished) as finished, date_trunc('minute',
finished-started) as duration from req where process not like 'reference' order by name;


-    Copy and paste output into Excel.
-    Add the times in table format to the Timing description page, ensuring that the
     request order is the same as in the Request list.
     •   Use the Text-to-Columns function in Excel to separate the table copied from the
         terminal window.
-    Change the date columns to the day-month-year format (e.g., 1-Jan-2014) in Excel
     as needed.
     •   May need to remove extra spaces before the request name and the date
         columns in order to properly edit the values.


    TrueAllele® Casework SOP        Cybergenetics Ó 2024                   Page 82 of 116




                                             003777
-    Be sure formatting is consistent. Note: some requests can finish in less than a day.
     Only include requests used for reporting. Omit screening requests.
-    Add horizontal lines as needed for clarity (make sure they are consistent with
     Request listing table).
-    Copy and paste timing information from Excel into Request.docx file.
-    Use the database query to gather the total duration time (in days, fractions of hours)
     for the requests used for reporting:
     •   If needed, log in to case World in terminal following steps above.
     •   Enter the database query:


select extract(epoch from (select sum(finished-started) from req where name like '%req
names%')/3600/24) as total_days;


     •   Paste the results into a spreadsheet program.
     •   Calculate hours using the following formula:


= round((MOD(total_days,1)*24),0)


     •   Copy and paste the days and hours output into the duration total field of
         Request.docx file.
     •   Enter \q to quit PostgreSQL.

11.6 Demonstrative Aid
Overview
A demonstrative aid is often needed for court to explain the science and results of the
TrueAllele® Casework system. This demonstrative aid is a PowerPoint presentation
that is created using a template. The presentation teaches the jury about the TrueAllele
science and what the case results mean. This section describes the procedures and
thought process behind preparing a demonstrative aid.




    TrueAllele® Casework SOP       Cybergenetics Ó 2024                 Page 92 of 116




                                            003787
Procedure
The demonstrative aid begins with a PowerPoint template. To prepare the case specific
demonstrative aid, the reporting scientist can choose a locus, capture data and interface
images, and prepare each slide, as outlined below.


Locus selection
Choosing a locus involves reviewing the data, genotypes, match statistics, and forensic
questions. A representative locus easily shows how TrueAllele works and fits with the
proposed number of contributors. This locus is used throughout the presentation to
illustrate what a DNA mixture looks like and the TrueAllele genotype inference process.
Exceptions can be made to the locus selection procedure for ease of creating a
demonstrative aid useful for teaching.


Procedure:


-    In the VUIer Report module, load the case’s report spec file or reported genotypes of
     interest.
-    Select the reported request, reference of interest, and the associated (or minimum)
     population.
     •   If not already identified (i.e., when reporting the average genotype and match
         statistic values for a comparison), identify a representative genotype from the
         concordant set with a log(LR) closest to the average for demonstrative purposes.
-    Open the Data View window for the reported request.
-    Open the Genotype View and Match View interfaces.
-    Examine each locus for the following criteria:
     •   A clearly explained pattern and number of peaks that fits the contributor
         assumption reported on.
     •   Good allele separation and balance.




    TrueAllele® Casework SOP        Cybergenetics Ó 2024                  Page 93 of 116




                                             003788
     •   Only a few inferred evidence genotype possibilities (if there are many, use a
         confidence level of 0.95 or lower as needed) with reasonable probability on the
         reference of interest’s genotype.
     •   For inclusionary match statistics, good information gain (but not the highest or
         lowest locus LR).
     •   For exclusionary match statistics, reasonable ratio between genotype brown and
         blue bars.
         o Ensure reference allele pair is included at the set confidence level.
-    If choosing a representative locus is difficult, discuss the locus choices with the
     reporting scientist or other staff to determine which example best represents the
     case.


Title slide
The Title slide introduces the case name, the date, the location of the trial, and the
person that is presenting the demonstrative aid.


Procedure:


-    Replace <Prosecution> with the name of the prosecuting body.
-    Replace <Defendant> with the first and last names of the defendant(s) from the
     Cybergenetics case report.
-    Replace <Month> with the month in which the trial will take place. Verify that the
     correct year is indicated.
     •   If the trial month is unknown, list the month and year the aid is being prepared.
-    Replace <City> and <State> with the city name and state abbreviation where the
     trial will take place.
-    Replace <Reporting Scientist> with the name of the person testifying with their
     associated <Degrees> following the name.
-    Center the text boxes as needed.


    TrueAllele® Casework SOP        Cybergenetics Ó 2024                   Page 94 of 116




                                             003789
DNA biology
The DNA biology slide explains the basics of cell biology and where DNA is found in a
cell. A locus is described as well.

Procedure: This slide does not change.


Short tandem repeat
The Short tandem repeat slide explains the concept of locus repeat units (alleles).

Procedure: This slide does not change; Replace with the UK version as appropriate.


DNA genotype
The DNA genotype slide explains a genetic locus, alleles, and genotypes. It also
explains why a person’s genotype is unique.


Procedure: This slide does not change.


DNA evidence interpretation
The DNA evidence interpretation slide provides a basic outline of how easily single
source DNA evidence is analyzed, interpreted, and compared to a reference. This is a
good introduction before mixtures complicate matters.


Procedure: This slide does not change.


DNA mixture interpretation
The DNA mixture interpretation slide describes how mixtures complicated interpretation
and are not as easy as single source DNA. Probabilities are also introduced.


Procedure: This slide does not change.




  TrueAllele® Casework SOP        Cybergenetics Ó 2024                 Page 95 of 116




                                           003790
Computers can use all the data
The Computers can use all the data slide is the first time any EPG case data appears in
the presentation. It explains what DNA data looks like at a locus and that there is a
pattern associated with the peaks.


Procedure:


-    Open the Data window for the reported/representative request (from the report
     notes).
-    Go to the locus that was selected for the demonstrative aid.
-    Turn on the peak and axis labels if they are not already visible.
-    Increase the font size to the maximum value.
-    Make the window a small square in the corner of the screen using the view buttons.
-    Increase the display cutoff to remove baseline labels as needed.
-    Use the Zoom tool to focus on the peaks of interest (including any stutter peaks),
     leaving about a peak’s width of space on either side.
-    Using a screenshot tool, select the portion of the window containing the data, axes
     and labels and save the image.
-    Insert the image into the PowerPoint slide.
-    Resize it to a height of 5”, align it to the bottom, and center it horizontally.
-    Indicate what is meant by peak height and peak size using the arrows and labels
     •   Choose a lower peak near the center of the image.
     •   Arrows should not cross through any peak labels.
     •   Arrows should touch and center on the peak label box.
-    Change <locus> to the full name of the locus that was used.


People may use less of the data (optional)
The People may use less of the data slide explains how DNA data is interpreted using
human methods. This slide is used when a non-TrueAllele match statistic will also be
presented at the trial; otherwise, it is typically removed.

    TrueAllele® Casework SOP         Cybergenetics Ó 2024                     Page 96 of 116




                                              003791
Procedure:


-    Copy data image from previous slide and paste onto this slide. This should place
     the image in the same position on the slide.
-    Move the red line so that it is at the stochastic threshold used by the laboratory that
     generated the data, and move the text ‘Threshold’ next to it. If this value is
     unknown, use 100 or 150 rfu (or some other reasonable value).
-    Place a red ‘x’ over the peak labels below the red line.
-    Place the solid blue boxes below the line on the peaks over threshold, and align
     them horizontally. Make these boxes to fit between the threshold and bottom of the
     peaks.
-    Place blue circles around the peak labels over the line, centering the label inside the
     circle.
-    Use the blue arrows to point from the “Over threshold…” text box to the blue circles.
-    Use the purple arrows to point from the “Under threshold…” text box to the red x’s.
-    If needed, move the “All-or-none…” and “Under threshold…” text boxes so they do
     not cover the peaks or axis labels.


How the computer thinks (Good explanation)
This How the computer thinks slide explains how TrueAllele interprets the DNA
evidence using a good explanation of the data. The computer considers every
genotype solution and tries to explain the peak pattern.


Procedure:


-    Copy data image from previous slide and paste onto this slide. This should place
     the image in the same position on the slide.
-    If needed, arrange the text boxes (except the title and subtitle) so that they do not
     cover the peaks and axis labels.
-    Indicate which alleles belong to the first contributor (who the story is focuses on):

    TrueAllele® Casework SOP        Cybergenetics Ó 2024                   Page 97 of 116




                                             003792
     •   Move the first set of colored boxes (usually blue) so that they encompass the
         contributor’s alleles and align them horizontally so that they are just touching the
         baseline (if possible). The boxes should be the same height.
     •   For exclusionary match statistics, the person of interest’s allele pair does not
         have to be included.
-    Indicate which alleles belong to the second contributor. When possible, add
     additional contributors in decreasing mixture weight.
     •   Move the second set of colored boxes so that they encompass the second
         contributor’s alleles and align them horizontally as above. The boxes should be
         the same height.
-    Indicate which alleles belong to the third contributor.
     •   Move the third set of colored boxes so that they encompass the third
         contributor’s alleles and align them horizontally as above. The boxes should be
         the same height.
-    Add boxes for additional contributors as needed.
-    Once all boxes are added, create the “animation” by copying and pasting this slide
     before itself and removing contributor boxes one by one until there are as many
     slides as the contributor assumption.
     •   For example, with 3 contributors, copy and paste the slide and remove the third
         set boxes leaving only the first two. Then, copy and paste that slide and remove
         the second set of boxes leaving only the first. There are now 3 slides that add up
         to the final proposal (i.e., all 3 colored boxes present).


How the computer thinks (Worse explanation)
This How the computer thinks slide shows a worse explanation of the data that
TrueAllele may consider. This slide visually shows a different explanation of the data
than previously seen.




    TrueAllele® Casework SOP         Cybergenetics Ó 2024                  Page 98 of 116




                                              003793
Procedure:


-    Copy data image from previous slide and paste onto this slide. This should place
     the image in the same position on the slide.
-    Create a proposed pattern that does not resemble the data (stacked rectangles have
     different heights than the data peaks).
     •   Create a pattern that is feasible and reasonable, but unrelated to the data. Some
         rectangles should be placed where there is no or little data. However, use actual
         allele positions, not off-ladder sizes. The 'evidence genotype' slide may provide
         helpful allele pair options for contributor 1.
     •   Change the genotype for contributor 1 (blue rectangles, person of interest in
         match statistic) to a different allele pair.
     •   Change other contributor genotypes. Move the allele pairs around.
     •   Change the rectangle heights (contributor quantity).
-    If needed, arrange the text boxes (except the title and subtitle) so that they do not
     cover the peaks, colored rectangles, and axis labels.


Evidence genotype
The Evidence genotype slide introduces the genotype probability distribution inferred by
TrueAllele from the data presented in the previous slides. It also explains that the
process is completely objective.


Procedure:


-    In the VUIer Report module, uncheck all genotypes.
     •   Enable the representative genotype.
     •   Download and enable CYB_placeholder population (system60, World
         placeholder). This population will allow the blue bars in Genotype View to appear
         narrower for continuity with the following slides.
-    Set the appropriate co-ancestry coefficient, if necessary.
    TrueAllele® Casework SOP          Cybergenetics Ó 2024                 Page 99 of 116




                                                003794
-    Open the Genotype window.
-    Increase the font size to the maximum value and turn on the axis labels.
-    Make the window a small square in the corner of the screen using the view buttons.
     •   If there are many genotypes, it may be necessary to use a lower confidence
         interval or resize the window to remove some of the white space above them.
     •   Using a screenshot program, select the portion of the window containing the
         genotypes, axes and labels and save the image. Do not close the Genotype
         window.
-    Insert the image into the PowerPoint slide, align it to the bottom of the slide, center
     it, and resize it to a height of 5”.
-    In the VUIer Report module, open the evidence genotype table and find the
     probabilities for each allele pair possibility at that locus and list them as whole
     number percentages above the allele pair probability bar on the slide.


DNA match information
The DNA match information slides introduces the reference genotype. It explains how a
comparison is made and how match information is determined at a locus.


Procedure:


-    In the VUIer Report module, turn on one population.
     •   Use the population that gave the minimum match statistic, or the one that gives
         the log(LR) closest to zero.
     •   Use a screenshot program in the Genotype window to select the same portion of
         the window from the previous slide and save the image.
-    Insert the image into the PowerPoint slides, keeping it in the same position as the
     image on the Evidence genotype slide.
-    On the first DNA match information slide, copy and paste the allele pair probabilities
     from the Evidence genotype slide, keeping them in the same position.


    TrueAllele® Casework SOP           Cybergenetics Ó 2024                 Page 100 of 116




                                                003795
-    On the second DNA match information slide, keep only the probability of the blue bar
     at the reference of interest’s allele pair.
     •   On this same slide, type the probability of the allele pair in the reference
         population near the brown bar at the suspect’s allele pair. This value is found in
         the composite genotype table by enabling the population frequency in the Report
         Preferences window.
     •   Place the red box around the two bars at the suspect’s allele pair.
     •   Divide the blue bar percentage by the brown bar percentage and type the
         (rounded) ratio into the <ratio> field, and move it near the red box, preferably
         centered on the top of the red box.
     •   Adjust the blue arrow so it points from “Prob(evidence match)” to the top corner
         of the blue bar.
     •   Adjust the brown arrow so it points from “Prob(coincidental match)” to the top of
         the brown box.
     •   Copy and paste the equation text boxes onto the first DNA match information
         slide, keeping it in the same position.
     •   Note: If the comparison is made to the victim or other reference, change
         “suspect” in the subheading to “victim” or other reference role.


Match information at # loci
The Match information at # loci slide explains that what was done for the locus in the
previous slide is done at all loci, and that the product of the ratios forms the match
statistic.


Procedure:


-    Change the number of loci in the slide title to reflect the total loci used.
-    In the VUIer Report module, enable the reference genotype of interest, keeping
     enabled the previously selected evidence and population genotypes.
-    In the Match window, select Display linear scale.

    TrueAllele® Casework SOP          Cybergenetics Ó 2024                  Page 101 of 116




                                               003796
-    Open the locus table and copy the loci and locus scores for the population used in
     the DNA match information slide and paste into the upper left of the “locus_strength”
     Excel spreadsheet.
-    Save the chart as a picture by right-clicking within the plot.
-    Insert the image into the PowerPoint slide and center it horizontally and align it to the
     bottom.
-    Move the red box to the locus used in the previous slide and adjust it so that the box
     encompasses the entire bar and locus label.


Is the reference in the evidence?
The match statement slide contains the statement from the case report for the
evidence-to-reference match. The only match statement listed is the one that goes
along with the data and genotype story told in the previous slides.


Procedure:


-    Replace <suspect> in the title to the appropriate reference label.
-    Replace <evidence> with the evidence item description.
-    Replace <reference> with the name of the reference as it appears in the case report.
-    Replace <BLKLR>, <CAULR> and <HISLR> with the appropriate match statistics as
     listed in the report.
-    For inclusionary match statistics, remove the ‘< >’ from around the word <more>.
-    For exclusionary match statistics, replace <more> with the word less (italicized).
-    Ensure proper population names are listed.
-    If only one population is reported, delete the other statements.

11.7 Case DVD
Overview
The TrueAllele Case DVD provides a wealth of information regarding TrueAllele and
case specific results to both prosecution and defense attorneys. This ~ 4 GB DVD
provides education materials, validation studies, the VUIer software, and every case
specific file produced in the case. This DVD can be used to answer any question
lawyers may have regarding the TrueAllele analysis of a case. It also allows others to
explore the results themselves.


Materials
The following outline provides instructions for the typical DVD.

-    On Dropbox, make a copy of the TrueAllele_DVD template folder.

12.5 Genotype Concordance
Below are some genotype concordance factors that may be helpful.


 concordance                   feature
 concordant                    similar genotype probabilities inferred across independ-
                               ent replicate requests

                               replicate matching genotypes have similar mixture
                               weights
                               replicate genotype log(LR) match statistics are similar
                               (for example, within 2 ban)
                               replicate genotype LR contributor distributions form a
                               single cluster

 possibly non-concordant       different genotype probabilities inferred across inde-
                               pendent replicate requests

                               replicate matching genotypes have dissimilar mixture
                               weight
                               replicate genotype log(LR) match statistics are different
                               (for example, not within 2 ban)
                               replicate genotype LR contributor distributions form mul-
                               tiple clusters



12.6 Assigning Genotypes
When assigning genotypes to matches, one of two algorithms is used, depending on the
context of the results. Note that, regardless of algorithm used, concordance is assessed
for all replicate genotypes.


Algorithm 1, no reuse of genotypes


This algorithm is used with validation studies and most casework. In this algorithm, each
inferred genotype is used only once.


  TrueAllele® Casework SOP       Cybergenetics Ó 2024                  Page 115 of 116




                                          003810
-    Determine the greatest match between the inferred and reference genotypes across
     all references.
-    Note the reference genotype for this match.
-    In the replicate request, identify the greatest match between the inferred genotypes
-    and this reference.
-    Remove these inferred genotypes (and reference) from the set and repeat until all
     references are matched.


Algorithm 2, with reuse of genotypes


This algorithm is used with casework when considering kinship where an inferred
genotype can be used more than once. As kinship genotypes are similar, they may, in
some circumstances, produce positive matches to the same inferred genotype.
-    Determine the greatest match between the inferred and reference genotype.
-    Note the inferred genotype.
-    In the replicate request, identify the greatest match between the inferred genotypes
     and this reference.
-    Remove this reference from the set and repeat.

         Sy Ray, may testify for the defense as an expert regarding cell towers, drive test,

geolocation, mobile device forensic extractions, call detail records, and software that is used to

interpret this data. Mr. Ray’s opinion/testimony will be based on his experience, education,

and trainings as detailed in his curriculum vitae which is included with this response as Exhibit

D11-C.

         This response serves to supplement the information in the Report attached as

Exhibit D11-B, photographs and/or video, drive test data, and related reports or past

testimony as previously discovered to the State on January 9, 2025. Below is a summary

of Mr. Ray’s anticipated testimony but does not repeat all specific findings that are

detailed in his report. It is anticipated that Mr. Ray may testify in the following areas:

         1. Interpretation of Drive Test Data and mapping supplied by the State.

         2. Analysis of call detail records.

         3. Geolocation Data review and analysis.

         4. Opinions regarding the FBI “Draft” CAST Report and “Final” CAST Report.


          This disclosure is provided as a summary. Further detail about the scope and breadth

 of his testimony may be found in his report and his curriculum vitae. Mr. Ray may offer

 testimony to refute any expert opinion not yet disclosed by the State.

          Case Report State of Idaho vs. Bryan C. Kohberger, Case Number CR29-22-2805
                                -




                                                            Analysis and Report by Sy Ray
Synopsis:

In October of 2023, was retained by the attorneys for Bryan Kohberger as an expert in the
                        |




field of cell towers, drive test, geolocation, mobile device forensic extractions, call detail
records, and software that is used to interpret this data. was contacted by Tom Slovenski of
Cellular Forensics in reference to a technical question he had involving call detail records.
Mr. Slovenski has completed the ZetX Subject Matter Expert (SME) course and is a
recognized SME in this field. It is common for me to receive calls from recognized SMEs
pertaining to technical questions arising from the analysis of call detail records. Mr.
Slovenski did not provide any case information other than there was a Non dissemination
Order issued by the court on this particular case, and he could not discuss case details. His
question pertained to drive test data collected by the FBI CAST team. Mr. Slovenski voiced
some concern as to the accuracy of the data and the ability to verify it. explained to him          |




would need to review the raw data in order to provide an opinion to the accuracy of the data.
Mr. Slovenski stated he would speak with the defense attorney to see if it was possible for
me to view the data.

On October 27, 2023, signed a confidentiality agreement to allow me to review the data in
                                |




this case. It was at this time discovered the case was regarding State of Idaho vs. Bryan C.
                                    |




Kohberger, Case Number CR29-22-2805.

Over the course of November 2023, was granted access to evidence that was in the
                                        |




possession of the defense. The evidence reviewed was mainly in reference to call detail
                                            |




records, mobile device forensic extracts, mobile device geolocation data, police reports,
drive test and FBI CAST report, timelines, surveillance video, and financial records.

One of the first areas was asked to address was to review and assist in the interpretation of
                            |




the drive test data. focused on the available drive test data collected by the FBI. Initially,
                    |




the only data had access to from the FBI drive test was contained in the FBI CAST "Draft"
              |




report and what was briefly mentioned in Special Agent             PowerPoint "report". The
"Draft" report is dated July 10, 2023. Special Agent            report, PowerPoint was the
only summary of the drive test, and is dated "02/15/23".

The report states drive test data was collected between November 16, 2022 and January 6,
2023. The report states the data was collected by both Special Acen               and Special
Agent            The areas focused on are vague, described only as Moscow, Pullman and
"south of" those towns. The report does state the raw files were enclosed in Special Agent
           original report. The raw files are critical for any analysis. learned the raw files
                                                                       |




had not been disclosed by the State and requested the files be obtained for further review.

In reviewing Mr. Kohberger's ATT call detail records and the FBI CAST "Draft" report,               |




immediately became concerned as to the accuracy of the drive test mapping. Specifically,
the shaded areas representing "coverage" found on slides 112,116, and 120. In comparing
commonly seen handoff data in Mr. Kohberger's ATT records, the coverage areas depicted in
                                                                                        DEFENDANT'S

the FBI CAST "draft" report are severely flawed. Further analysis would require access to the

In further review of the "Draft" report,  also noted several other areas of concern. The
                                                   |




mapping of tower connections provide in the "Draft" report was missing significant data from
the AT&T call detail records. On average, more than 90% of the available data was not

creates a number of issues as to the accuracy of both the analysis and related report.

                     |




at this point of my analysis was the appearance that the missing/flawed data was
exculpatory in nature to Mr. Kohberger.

                                                                                  |

details that analysis.

SECTION 2 METHODOLOGY FOR REVIEW AND ANALYSIS OF DATA
            -




In the United States, cell phone providers collect and maintain certain records that can be
used to help determine a mobile device's general location at a specific time. This type of
data is referred to as Geolocation Data.

The specificity as to the precise location of a device can greatly vary when working with
geolocation data. It is critical in any geolocation analysis to consider known accuracy and
error rates within the type of data being analyzed as well as the methodology used to conduct
the analysis.

For this analysis,   |   received 3 different type of geolocation data from AT&I, T-Mobile, and
Verizon.

       Cell Site/Cell Sector Data        this geolocation data provides a log of connection
                                         -




       "sessions" in which a connection time, the type of connection made (voice, SMS, or
       data), duration of the connection, and the location of the cell site and antenna array
       (sector) used by the cell site to make the connection. Some types of cell site/cell
       sector data include what is known as handoff data. Handoff data is when more than
       one cell site/cell sector is used by the device during a single session. For example, a
       mobile device establishes a 5-minute session with the AT&T network while driving on
       a freeway. During the session, the AT&T network maintains a constant connection
       from the network to the device by "handing off" the connection from one cell site/cell
       sector to another while driving on the freeway. When records are received with
       handoff data it is a well-established best practice to analyze the handoff data, as it
       will help provide specific details in reference to movement of the device, direction of
       movement, stagnation, and enhanced location estimations.

       Timing Data this geolocation data provides similar data as the cell site/cell location
                         -




       data with the addition of a distance measurement. This distance measurement is an
       estimated distance from the cell site to the mobile device during the connection.
       When carefully analyzed, this type of data can be some of the most precise data
       received from providers in regards to device location. When multiple cell sites are
       connected to by the device in a short period of time, the timing measurements
       provide a form of trilateration, providing very precise device location information.

       AT&T Historical Precision Location Information Data "ReportLoc"                  this
                                                                                        -




       geolocation data is proprietary to AT&T, only being available from AT&T. This data is
       an estimated location of the device, presented in latitude and longitude format with
       a "range". The "range" is intended to give an accuracy reading to the data, implying
       the device should be with "X" meters of the latitude and longitude point. These
       "ranges" will vary between 25 meters and over 30,000 meters. There are several
       documented cases where this data is extremely inaccurate and will produce false
       data. As an example, there is an instance in this case where a device is reported to


                                                 11

                                               003835
          Case Report – State of Idaho vs. Bryan C. Kohberger, Case Number CR29-22-2805
                                                              Analysis and Report by Sy Ray
       be in Seattle and New Orleans at the same time based on “precision location
       information data”. The accuracy of this data can be signiﬁcantly impacted by device
       activity. For example, when an application is running on the device that requires GPS,
       the accuracy of the data in this report dramatically increases. In cases where the
       device is running an open version of a map application, capturing GPS, it is common
       to see 25-meter locations that will perfectly align with the travel of the device to such
       an extent it is mathematically impossible for the locations to be random or
       inaccurate.

In cases where all three types of data described above is available for analysis, all three types
of data should be used for analysis. The dieerent data sets can often corroborate each other
and provide an enhanced understanding of device behaviors and movements. Based on my
review of the State’s Discovery, it does not appear anyone has done a complete analysis with
all of the data available.

In this analysis, I converted all the geolocation data described above into mappable ﬁles.
The mappable ﬁles are created in Keyhole Markup Language (kml.kmz), allowing the work
product to be review by anyone with a computer and free version of Google Earth. The
connections were synced to data and time allowing for the animation of device patterns over
time. Each device was assigned to a speciﬁc color to allow anyone to identify and follow a
speciﬁc device. Once mapped, I viewed each data set independently as well as with other
devices to establish patterns of life and possible device interactions. In going through this
process, all of my work is documented and preserved for peer review and critique as needed.
It should be noted this type of documentation is a common, well-established practice
throughout the law enforcement community. Documenting the methodology used, ﬁndings,
conclusions, follow up requests, and ﬁnalized work product is the only way to present a work
product that can be properly presented for peer review and/or critique.

As a point of concern, I am completing this report without the beneﬁt of having receiving
completed work from the State’s Expert(s) as it relates to methodology and opinion. Reports
associated with the call detail record analysis are overly vague, incomplete, and generally
contain no substantive value. Raw mapping ﬁles utilized by the State have not been
disclosed, if they were ever created. Extremely poor record management further
complicates the issue as records have not been organized into any meaningful structure. In
working on criminal investigations for over 25 years, the evidentiary process used in this case
is one of the most chaotic I have worked with. As such, it is possible some of the missing
information/data I refer to in this report exists, but I have been unable to ﬁnd it.

In my analysis, I focused on the following:

   §   Connections between Mr. Kohberger and any of the deceased’s and/or associates of
       the deceased (common call report).

                  Mr. Kohberger to any of the decedents is a cornerstone of this
                  investigation.

                  State to support any meaningful analysis on this point.

       o While I have identiﬁed locations Mr. Kohberger and the deceased(s)
         frequented in common (common stores located in a small community), I am

    from those records.

SECTION 3 – DRIVE TEST DATA REVIEW

The term “Drive Test” refers to the physical act of taking cellular network survey equipment
into the ﬁeld to analyze cellular signals at any given location. By repeating this process over
and over throughout an area, it is possible to determine cellular coverage areas with a high
degree of certainty. The practice is well accepted both in the engineering and network
planning ﬁelds as well as criminal justice applications involving geolocation analysis. Over
the course of my career, I have performed 100s, if not over a 1000 of these “drive tests.” I
have always utilized the Rohde and Schwarz TSMx network survey tools to perform these
tests. These network tools are utilized daily by network engineers around the world.

By way of background and training, I have received signiﬁcant training from Rohde and
Schwarz on the TSMx products. I maintained a business relationship with Rohde and
Schwarz for over 8 years. During this relationship my company was the sole provider of
Rohde and Schwarz TSMx tools to State and Local law enforcement throughout the United
States. This required me to provide training and ﬁeld assistance to law enforcement on the
product line. In addition to this, I worked directly with Rohde and Schwarz engineers on
developing new features and software enhancements on the product line. This relationship
has allowed me to review and analyze 1000s of drive tests in the course of my daily work.

FBI CAST utilizes a drive test product from Gladiator Forensics. It is important to note that
while the product is purchased through Gladiator, the internal survey equipment powering
the tool is manufactured by Rohde and Schwarz as well. Gladiator does utilize another
software platform to analyze the raw data collected by the survey equipment. Thus, there
are two components to drive testing. The physical survey equipment, manufactured by

analysis, utilized the Rohde and Schwarz "Nestor" software. FBI CAST utilized the Gladiator
         |

utilized by this product is proprietary to Gladiator. The software component takes the raw

It is both important and necessary to understand the raw drive test data consists of nothing
more than latitude and longitude points with network survey readings. Any process that
takes that raw data and converts it into a shape ﬁle beyond those latitude and longitude
points should be subject to scientiﬁc review. In this case, the FBI CAST process is to use the
Gladiator GAR program to make this conversion. I am unaware of and unable to ﬁnd any
scientiﬁc documentation by Gladiator on how this is done. I spoke with Gladiator Forensic,
Rick Zemlock. He wasn’t sure if there was any published data that could be reviewed to test
and analyze the results provided by the FBI CAST team in this case. I followed up with a
detailed email to Mr. Zemlock requesting any documentation they may be in possession of
or aware of that would allow for independent testing and evaluation of the GAR mapping
process. Mr. Zemlock did email me back explaining the only document he could “point me
towards” is the Gladiator Patent - Patent number: 8892120, Filed: Dec 13, 2011, Date of
Patent: Nov 18, 2014, Patent Publication Number: 20130150074, Assignee: Gladiator
Innovations, LLC (Melbourne, FL), Application Number: 13/324,967.

While I can appreciate Gladiator’s desire to protect their intellectual properties with a
patent, it does not satisfy the requirement of providing some type of scientiﬁc
documentation on the actual process used by the GAR platform. In fact, the patent data is
overwhelming vague on any real process used by the Gladiator tool. Additionally, the type of
network connections associated with this investigation were not even in service in 2011
when the patent was ﬁled. Given this, it is safe to say there is no information available nor is
Gladiator Forensics willing to provide information that would allow for a proper, independent
review. Any “peer review” of this data without such information is ﬂawed.

In the course of my analysis,   |   noted the following issues:

       Missing Data

       Data is collected by physically driving the survey equipment around in a vehicle. As
       with any survey technique, it takes time to receive, analyze, and store the data being
       collected. This collection process and the time it takes to properly perform it requires
       the user/operator to be mindful of the speed they are traveling and to monitor the
       equipment performance at the same time. If driving too fast, the survey equipment
       can fall behind and not properly collect the data required. In reviewing the raw data
       provided by the FBI, it appears this error occurred on at least one occasion. As a
       result, there are several miles of data collection that went missed.

       Coverage maps were created in both of the CAST "Draft" report and "Final" report that
       included the area where the missing data mentioned above is relevant. Given the
       coverage map was Created, it is assumed Special Agent                an d/or Special
       Agen           were unaware of the missing data. This is assumed as it is logical to
       expect them to rescan the area in the event they were aware of the missing data.
       Given can find no evidence of the area being rescanned, must assume they are
             |                                                       |




       unaware of their error.

       The error significantly impacts the purported coverage area represented for eNode
       424199-15 in both the "Draft" and "Final" reports. The coverage area depicted in the
       reports is significantly undersized (by over 3 miles). Essentially, by attempting to
       create a coverage area with raw data missing critical measurements, areas of
       possible coverage cannot be considered by the software. This is the result of a user
       error in the drive test process. As a best practice, it is recommended operators

       there are collection issues and prevents this error from occurring.

            Handoffs allow a mobile device to seamlessly jump from one cell site/sector to
            another to maintain a constant connection to the cellular network. As a guiding
            principle of handoffs, a mobile device can only handoff to another cell site/sector that
            is providing coverage to the location where the handoff occurs. In any given area
            within the networks coverage area, multiple cell sites/sectors provide overlapping
            coverage.

            In Bryan Kohberger's AT&T cell detail records there are thousands of handoffs
            reported. In analyzing these handoffs, there are numerous handoffs occurring in the
            records that would be physically impossible based on the FBI CAST Drive Test
            Mapping. There are repeating handoffs seen throughout the records where
            overlapping coverage between two cell sites/sectors must exist, yet in the FBI drive
            test coverage maps, these cell sites/sectors do not overlap.

In reviewing any analysis of geolocation data, there is a need to identify missing data that

analysis. Albeit a normal part of my analysis, my findings as it related to missing data is

As explained in the methodology section of this report, common data source used in
                                                               Cca




geolocation analysis is timing reports from the cell phone carriers. Prior to November 2022,
all of the major cell phone carriers were providing timing reports. The process of obtaining
these reports and the retention periods of the reports would vary from carrier to carrier.
Some carriers, like AT&T, would also limit what agencies could obtain these reports. In
December of 2022, the FBI CAST members did have access to AT&T timing reports. The
retention period for these reports from AT&T range from 60 to 90 days. have prior history
                                                                             |




working with these reports and have seen timing reports from AT&T with 45 days of history
prior to November of 2022.

In this case investigators requested and reviewed numerous phones for various reasons.


       Phone records, to include timing reports were obtained on all four of the decedents.

       Phone records, to include timing reports were obtained on the other roommates,
       Bethany Funke and Dylan Mortensen.

       Phone records for two investigative leads develop early in case were obtained, to
       include timing records for Jack Showalter and Jack Ducouer.

       One of the devices identified to be in the immediate area of the crime scene just
       before the crime belonged to Molly McMichaels. Investigators obtained her phone
       records, to include timing data.

Essentially, investigators requested and received timing data for all the cell phone records
they requested with geolocation. There is one exception to this, investigators requested, but
allegedly did not receive timing data for Mr. Kohberger. It was explicitly requested in two
different search warrants, but allegedly was not provided by AT&I. The accuracy and
completeness of AT&T timing reports around this time (November/December 2022) make
them incredibly powerful investigative tools. Special Agent                well aware of this and
has made requesting and using them a standard operating procedure, as he demonstrated
in this case. It is inconceivable to this investigator Special Agent           would not use Mr.
Kohberger's AT&T timing reports.     In the event there is any doubt to Special Agent
claims in his report, the timing report would be the best way to show accuracy. Conversely,
if Special Agent                report is full of errors, the timing report would immediately
highlight those errors.   It is because of these reasons do believe Mr. Kohberger's timing
                                                           |




report was obtained in this investigation in the same manner the other 9 timing reports were.
| do believe the timing report was in stark contrast to Special Agent                 report, but
more importantly the false timeline of events purported in search warrant affidavits. For
these reasons, Mr. Kohberger's timing report was concealed. The exculpatory nature of this
report cannot be overlooked.

SUMMARY

In completing my analysis,     |   found the following:

   1.   The cell phone geolocation reports provided by the State in this investigation are
        intentionally misleading, plagued with omitted exculpatory evidence, and cannot be
        relied on to the slightest degree.

   2.   The absence of work product can only be attributed to one of two things an         -




        overwhelmingly incompetent analysis or intentional concealment to hide
        exculpatory evidence.

   3.   Mr. Kohberger's AT&T records provide significant detail as it relates to his geolocation
        pattern of life. The State's investigation is completely void of these patterns. can
                                                                                           |




        find no reference to Mr. Kohberger's pattern of life in any report despite demanding 6
        months of AT&T records to establish such a pattern. The reason for this is clear to this
        investigator, as that pattern of life is tremendously exculpatory for Mr. Kohberger.

             a. He routinely drives in random locations late at night and early in the morning.
             b. He is constantly cycling the power on his phone for different periods of time.
             c. His daily geolocation patterns are chaotic. Random travel patterns are
                 normal.

   4.   Investigators relied heavily on inaccurate analysis to establish probable cause in
        nearly every search warrant affidavit issued to secure evidence against Mr. Kohberger.
        These inaccuracies are to such an extent, any geolocation subject matter expert

Case History

In October of 2023, Roloff Digital Forensics (RDF) was retained by Ms. Anne Taylor, esq. to assist in
her representation of Mr. Bryan Kohberger.

Examiner and Firm Background

I am the President and Senior Digital Forensics Examiner at Roloff Digital Forensics, LLC, a private
digital forensics firm with headquarters in Spokane, Washington. RDF provides digital forensics
services and consulting on legal matters that deal with electronic evidence.

My educational background includes a professional certificate in computer forensics from Oregon
State University and New Technologies, Inc. (NTI), the Certified Computer Examiner (CCE)
certification from the International Society of Forensic Computer Examiners, the EnCase Certified
Examiner (EnCE) certification previously by Guidance Software (now OpenText), the Cellebrite
Certified Logical Operator (CCLO) certification, the Cellebrite Certified Physical Analyst (CCPA)
certification, the Cellebrite Certified Mobile Examiner (CCME) certification, an associate degree in the
applied science of network engineering from Spokane Community Colleges and a bachelor degree in
liberal studies with an emphasis in program management from Whitworth University. Currently, I am
serving on the Board of Advisors for the International Society of Forensic Computer Examiners.

I have been working exclusively in the field of digital forensics since 2003. During this time I have
conducted examinations on thousands of pieces of digital evidence to include: hard drives, compact
discs (CDs), digital versatile discs (DVDs), floppy diskettes, thumb drives, flash cards, magnetic tapes,
tablet devices, cellular phones, subscriber identity module (SIM) cards, electronic medical records
(EMRs), personal digital assistants (PDAs), smart phones, feature phones, and data derived from
service providers such as Internet Service Providers, “Cloud” storage providers, and cellular service
providers. During my work within the digital forensic field, I have completed well over fifteen hundred
cases which consisted of analyzing the previously referenced media types and/or data maintained on
such devices.

I frequently lecture on the topic of general digital as well as mobile forensics and how it can be applied
in the legal system. In 2015, I co-authored the chapter mobile forensics for the Chapman and
Hall/CRC publication of Mobile Devices: Tools and Technologies. I have been recognized as a
computer, digital, and mobile forensics expert witness as well as an expert in cell site location

                                                  003885
information analysis (CSLI) in numerous United States district courts, United States military courts
and state courts throughout the country.

My firm’s list of clients in these matters includes the United States Navy, United States Marine Corps,
United States Army, United States Air Force, United States Coast Guard, federal and state public
defender offices throughout the United States and private attorneys throughout the United States.

I and members of my firm have investigated digital evidence in allegations of homicide, sexual
exploitation, solicitation, assault, unauthorized systems access, voyeurism, medical malpractice, forgery,
unauthorized use, espionage, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, drug trafficking, credit card
trafficking and identity theft, threats against the president, his family and staff, and robbery, to name a
select few categories.

                                 003969
                                       TOM SLOVENSKI

        Tom Slovenski, Forensic Cellular LLC, may testify for the defense as an expert

regarding cellular forensics, which includes but in no way is limited to cell phone towers.

                          AUTHOR’S BACKGROUND


The Author, Thomas J. Slovenski, is the owner and chief analyst for Cellular
Forensics, LLC, located in Greenville County, South Carolina. The Author is a
former police officer and detective with 15 years of experience. During his tenure,
the Author worked in patrol, the detective division, and the internal affairs division.
After retiring from a police career, the Author secured training and certification in
Mobile Forensics in 2007 and Cell Tower Records and Geolocation Analysis from

                                                                                     1

                                         003971
2009 to the present. In 2007, the author formed Cellular Forensics, LLC, supplying
mobile forensic examinations and expert testimony in mobile phone data acquisition,
mobile spyware discovery, cell tower records, and geolocation analysis to law
enforcement and criminal defense. The Author is also a Licensed Private
Investigator with the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) with
license number PDC2073 since 2002. In total, the Author has over thirty-five (35)
years of investigative experience.


Since 2007, the Author has produced fourteen (14) articles on mobile forensics and
three (3) authored books on Mobile Forensics. The Author has been employed by
the United States Department of State as a senior digital forensics instructor to
foreign national police agencies under the Anti-Terrorism Assistance Act (ATA)
Program. The Author has taught hundreds of police officers, insurance investigators,
judges, and attorneys in mobile forensics and cell tower forensics worldwide.


Additionally, the Author has created, produced, and appeared in eight (8) training
videos on Mobile Forensics for the South Carolina Bar for their CEU Program.
These videos were provided for national use and have been viewed nationally by
attorneys for Continuing Education Credits.


The Author has been recognized by numerous courts across America as an Expert
Witness and has testified in various high-profile homicide cases.


The Author is certified by the LexisNexis Corporation as a Subject Matter Expert
(SME) and continues his certification each year by attending the necessary
classroom instruction mandated for such a title. The Author has been a certified
Subject Matter Expert in Call detail Records and Geolocation Analysis since 2017.
                                                                                  2

                                       003972
Before this training, Affiant was certified in 2009 and 2011 by Cellular Data
Resources in cell tower records analysis. The Author has 17 years of training and
first-hand experience in Call Detail Records and Geolocation Analysis.


The Author has worked cases with both the prosecution and the defense and has been
consulted by various law enforcement agencies and attorneys. Hereafter, the Author

shall be referred to as "this Analyst" for the remainder of this report.




                                 CASE ANALYSIS


On October 10, 2023, this Analyst was contracted by Attorney Anne Taylor of Idaho

regarding the case of the State of Idaho vs. Bryan Kohberger. This Analyst was
requested by Attorney Anne Taylor to analyze many and various CDRs including
the AT&T Call Detail Records pertaining to mobile telephone number:

8458.



According to AT&T, the mobile telephone           numbers458 is registered to
Bryan C. Kohberger of Albrightsville, Pennsylvania, and has been an active number
since June 23, 2022. Additionally, the device utilizing this mobile number according
to AT&T records is a "Samsung, SM-S908U" with IMEI of 3509623774602317 and

IMSI number 310280052649401.


This Analyst was provided with Call Detail Records (herein referred to as "CDRs'')

pertaining to           s4ss (herein referred to as "xxx8458" device), which were
supplied to Attorney Taylor by the Latah County (Idaho) Prosecuting Attorney. The
date range for these records was from June 23, 2022 @ 23:33:18 hours through

                                                                                   3




                                         003973
December 24, 2022 @ 00:53:29 hours. AT&T Creation Date read “12/23/2022”
with the Run date showing “12/23/22” and the Run Time as “21:18:02”. Said
records were supplied in UTC time zone. Also supplied were various receipts of
Mr. Kohberger’s as well as pictures taken from a device used with mobile number
xxx8458. This analyst has vigorously analyzed these data records.


In addition, this Analyst was provided with other CDR data including:


   ● Chapin Verizon CDRs (number xxx1841)
   ● Ducoeur Verizon CDRs (number xxx2881)
   ● Funke Verizon CDRs (number xxx3185)
   ● Funke Charter Home Phone
   ● Goncalves T-Mobile CDRs and Timing Advance Records (number xxx4818)
   ● Mortensen T-Mobile CDRs and Timing Advance Records (number xxx4782)
   ● Kernodle AT&T CDRs and Timing Advance Records (number xxx1278)
   ● Mogen AT&T CDRs and Timing Advance Records (number xxx1224)
   ● Showalter AT&T CDRs and Timing Advance Records (number xxx7846)
   ● Cellebrite report on number xxx8458
   ● FBI Cast report (both Draft and Final)
   ● Grand Jury Exhibits


NOTE Regarding the Timing Advance Records above from AT&T:
AT&T’s Timing Advance Records are utilized by and for E911 services to provide
accurate readings to Law Enforcement in the event of an emergency.


However, after repeated efforts, the Defense was only able to secure three (3) of the
four (4) AT&T Timing Advance Records dealing with Kernodle, Mogen, Showalter,
                                                                                   4

                                        003974
and Mr. Kohberger. Mr. Kohberger’s Timing Advance Records were never
produced. What is strange is that all the above four (4) accounts are AT&T accounts.
The four Timing Advance Records were requested in Law Enforcement’s warrants
to AT&T. Yet Law Enforcement says Mr. Kohberger’s Timing Advance Records
are “not available”. This is very concerning as Timing Advance Records are
extremely accurate and could prove to be exculpatory evidence for Mr. Kohberger’s
defense.


During this Analyst’s investigations, this Analyst sought the assistance of Expert Sy
Ray and requested that he join the Defense Team. Mr. Ray was able to not only peer
review this Analyst’s work but also provide an invaluable source for data analysis
as well as real-time drive-by tower mapping and analysis. This Analyst refers the
reader to Mr. Ray’s work for further work product and his expert opinions.


The xxx8458 CDRs were processed by this Analyst using the TraX forensic mapping
software tool, which is a forensic CDR mapping program originally developed by
the ZetX Corporation and recently sold to LexisNexis. Since 2016, this Analyst has
used the TraX forensic mapping software due to its high scientific accuracy and
respect in the forensic community. Since starting forensic mapping of CDRs in
2009, all mapping by this Analyst was performed using Microsoft Streets and Trips.
Around the year 2016, Microsoft discontinued updating Streets and Trips leaving
the forensic community to search for an alternative. After thorough and careful
analysis of other forensic mapping software at that time, this Analyst subscribed to
the TraX software due to:


   1. Wide acceptance by Law Enforcement Agencies (both local, state, and
       federal)
                                                                                   5

                                        003975
   2. Daubert/Frye acceptance across the country
   3. The success rate of cases using this software
   4. Continuous training for all users
   5. Subject Matter Expert Certification offered
   6. Continual updates to the software
   7. Continual verification of cell towers’ locations, sectors, azimuths, etc.
   8. Outstanding customer service
   9. Subject Matter Experts within the company that would testify on the user’s
       behalf if needed
   10. Peer review by certified Subject Matter Experts
   11. Founder’s stance on speaking only to the data


Since his initial training in 2016 with the TraX software, in 2017 this Analyst was
awarded the Subject Matter Expert Certification by the ZetX (original owner of
TraX) company in Call Detail Record and Geolocation Analysis. This Analyst has
maintained this certification to this present date by attending yearly 40-hour classes
offered by the LexisNexis (present owners) corporation. This analyst is one of only
a few non-law enforcement examiners in the country with this certification from
LexisNexis.


Upon processing and mapping the xxx8458 CDRs, this Analyst was able to track the
movements of said device as it communicated with the area cell towers.


This Analyst was also provided with each of the victims’ CDRs as well as CDRs
belonging to friends of the victims. These CDRs were mapped and analyzed with
no connection found between the victims and friends, to the xxx8458 account.

           July 9, 2022: POOL PARTY WITH POINTS OF INTEREST


Using the xxx8458 CDRs supplied by Law Enforcement, this Analyst mapped the
device's movements from approximately 0013 hours on 7/9/22 to approximately
0120 hours on 7/10/22.


From approximately 0013 hours to approximately 1330 hours, xxx8458 utilized cell
towers covering the Pullman, Idaho, area and Mr. Kohberger's apartment, which is

also located in Pullman.



At approximately 1332 hours, the xxx8458 device used a tower south of Moscow,
Idaho, which covered an extensive area.


At approximately 1414 hours, the xxx8458 device utilized a tower located in
Moscow Idaho. This tower's coverage takes in TriState Outfitters and the Grove


                                                                                     7



                                          003977
Apartments, both located in Moscow Idaho. According to a receipt supplied by Mr.
Kohberger, Kohberger made a purchase at the TriState Outfitters at “2:08:27 PM.”
Then, from approximately 1418 to approximately 1518 hours, xxx8458 utilized a
tower south of Moscow Idaho that also provided coverage to TriState Outfitters and
the Grove Apartments.


Then from approximately 1518 to approximately 2223 hours, the xxx8458 device
continued to utilize the same tower. From 2223 hours on, the xxx8458 device
proceeded westbound utilizing various towers in Moscow, Idaho, and Pullman,
Washington until approximately 0120 hours on 7/10/22 when it used a tower
covering the Kohberger apartment.


See Exhibit “JULY 9 POOL PARTY” for a detailed presentation and a copy of the
receipt.

   July 12, 2022: MOSCOW MOUNTAIN WITH POINTS OF INTEREST


This Analyst was requested by the Defense to examine the supplied xxx8458 CDRs
for the date of July 12, 2022, regarding Mr. Kohberger reporting that he had made a
trip to Moscow Mountain and other points of interest.


The transactions between the cell towers and the xxx8458 device start on that date
at approximately 0101 hours, utilizing a cell tower which provides cell coverage to
the Kohberger apartment area. This device continued to utilize cell towers in the
Pullman, Washington area until approximately 1802 hours. Said device then appears
to move eastward and arrive in the area of Moscow Mountain at approximately 1815
                                                                                 8

                                       003978
hours. At approximately 1829 hours, the device itself reports taking a photograph
of the Moscow Mountain map. Then at approximately 1859 hours, the device
reports taking a photograph of foliage.


At approximately 2116 hours, the device is then seen proceeding westward and
arriving in the Pullman area at approximately 2223 hours. At approximately 2248
hours, the device utilized a cell tower that provides coverage to three businesses in
Pullman, Washington: Walmart, Safeway, and Sunset Mart.
According to the Walmart receipt provided by Mr. Kohberger, dated “07/12/22
22:47:07”, Mr. Kohberger purchased numerous items. Then, Mr. Kohberger made
another purchase at the Safeway. According to that receipt, his purchases were made
on “07/12/22 23:05”. Then Mr. Kohberger proceeded to the Sunset Mart, where a
receipt verifying purchases made by Mr. Kohberger, showed a purchase made on
“7/12/22 23:12”. It is to be noted that from approximately 2223 hours through
approximately 2323 hours, the xxx8458 device is utilizing several towers, all with
coverage of these three stores.


The cell tower data affirms Mr. Kohberger’s alibi of being on Moscow Mountain
and the store purchases on that date.


See Exhibit entitled “JULY 12 MOUNTAIN HIKE” for a detailed video
presentation and copies of said receipts.

           EXHAUSTIVE FBI CAST FINAL REPORT ANALYSIS

An exhaustive analysis was performed on the final FBI CAST report dated July 8,
2024. In this report, this Analyst notes how the CAST member has made the report
in a very general and yet confusing manner. Also of note is how CAST does not

properly provide and illustrate the many handoffs the xxx8458 device did with the
area towers. This left out key evidence. Also, the use of shaded areas and "pie" type

diagrams provide the less knowledgeable listener with confusion.         It is then the

CAST member who can lead the juror and court to the explanation the CAST
member himself wishes to give to enhance the story the Prosecution wants the court

to accept. This CAST report is prejudicial and slated to follow a theory of guilt and

not the actual data. Data doesn't lie, and what has been left out of this report is just

as important as what data was noted.   This report is not truly factual, with numerous
data points left out that could assist the Defendant's case and team.

                            AUTHOR'S EXPERT OPINION


This Analyst has exhaustively examined the AT&T Call Detail Records pertaining
to mobile number               45s as well as other cell tower data pertaining to the
victims and other persons.


The Expert opinion of this Analyst is as follows: there is no cell tower data presented

by Law Enforcement to the Defense that links the xxx8458 device to the King Road
murders.



What this Analyst has noted is a profound push by Law Enforcement to use these
Call Detail Records to paint a story that the data cannot support or prove. There is
no Cell Tower or GPS data presented to support the claim that the xxx8458 device

                                                                                     35


                                         004005
was at 1122 King Road, Moscow, Idaho, on November 13, 2022, from
approximately 3:00 am – 4:30 am.


What is disturbing is the LACK of actual data that was not made discoverable by
Law Enforcement. This data would be extremely helpful to the Defendant’s case.
There have been numerous omissions by the FBI CAST Agent. This is disturbing.
The data that was not shown is very exculpatory, and it appears that it was clearly
and intentionally left out of the CAST final report and other members of the Law
Enforcement team.


End of Report.

PURPOSE
The purpose of this report is to provide a forensic assessment relating to the
examination of available physical and behavioral evidence in the stabbing deaths of
Ethan J. Chapin, 20 YO WM; Xana A. Kernodle, 20 YO WF; Kaylee J. Goncalves, 21
YO WF; and Madison M. Mogen, 21 YO WF. These homicides were determined to have
occurred on November 13, 2022, in the early hours of the morning, just after 4am.
However, they were not reported to 911, by surviving housemate Bethany Funke and
Dylan Mortenson, until just before 12pm (noon) the same day. These homicides
occurred at 1122 King Rd., Moscow, Idaho — a three story rental house with at least
two rooms and a bathroom on each floor.

Specifically, this examiner was asked to conduct a Crime Scene Analysis of this
stabbing incident by defense counsel, Anne Taylor. Crime Scene Analysis is the process
of examining and interpreting the specific features of a crime, related crime scenes, and
relevant contextual information. It requires consideration of the complete forensic
investigation, to include context, forensic victimology1, and the subsequent examination
of available physical and behavioral evidence (e.g., crime reconstruction and Modus
Operandi). It can also be used to infer motive (see generally Coronado & Turvey, 2022;
Turvey, 2022; and UN, 2014).

As with any forensic examination, Crime Scene Analysis also requires an assessment
and consideration of the nature and quality of any underlying forensic investigation and
examinations. This is a crucial step in any scientific process, necessary to reliably
establish that due diligence by government agencies has resulted in a showing of
Evidence Integrity2, and an absence of negligence3. This scientific requirement also
accommodates the legal reality that every victim, and defendant, has the right to access
justice. This includes a competent investigation into the essential elements and




1 Forensic victimology is required as a foundational component in every death investigation (e.g., NIJ,

1999, 2011, & 2024 — Section E: Recording Decedent Profile Information).
2 Evidence integrity refers to the scientific reliability and subsequent court-worthiness of any evidence that

has been collected. It is demonstrated by adherence to basic protocols associated with establishing a
reliable chain of custody, the protection of physical evidence while it is in custody, and its competent
testing and interpretation by qualified forensic personnel. It also refers to any failure to collect, protect,
and/ or test essential items of evidence. In a scientific examination, evidence integrity may not be
assumed — rather it must be established. Otherwise reliable interpretations are not possible. See Bay
(2008), Crowder & Turvey (2017), Gardenier (2011), Turvey (2013), and Sweet v. Sisters of Providence
(1995).
3 Negligence refers to the failure to follow basic practice standards and protocols, resulting in a breach of

a professional’s duty of care. It can imply negligent action, as well as the failure to act. This is especially
true when the duty to take action is mandated by established agency policies, protocols, and related legal
rulings or statutes.
                                                                                          Brent E. Turvey, PhD
                                                                          CSA: Idaho vs. Bryan C. Kohberger
                                                                                                    Page 2 of 25

                                                     004027
evidence associated with the criminal charges brought by the state, by competent
forensic investigators and examiners4.

Collectively, this approach strengthens scientific reconstructions and related case theory
development. It also identifies areas where further investigation and forensic
examination may be needed. Additionally, limitations within the available evidence can
be identified to prevent or eliminate inappropriate and/or unfounded interpretations or
theories (see generally Chisum & Turvey, 2012; Crowder & Turvey, 2017; NIJ, 1999,
2011, 2013, & 2024; and Turvey, 2022; 2023).

MATERIALS EXAMINED
This examiner agreed to analyze the evidence in this case for Attorney Anne Taylor in
late October of 2024. Subsequently, this examiner began to receive related discovery
material from her office. Upon request, this examiner was provided with, and relied
upon, at least the following evidence to form the forensic conclusions offered in this
report:

    1. Related Security Camera videos and enhancements from the area of 1122 King
       Rd., Moscow, Idaho.
    2. The 911 call by Bethany Funke.
    3. Related law enforcement affidavits, warrants, and reports, to include: The
       Moscow Police Department, The Idaho State Police, and The Federal Bureau of
       Investigation.
    4. Related law enforcement photos, body cams, and videos.
    5. Related Forensic Investigation, Examination, Criminalistics Reports and photos.
    6. Autopsy reports of all four victims prepared by the OCME in Spokane, WA.
    7. Autopsy photos of all four victims prepared by the OCME in Spokane, WA.
    8. Related Cell Phone extractions.
    9. Related Law Enforcement witness interviews.

This list does not encompass the entirety of the discovery material provided to this
examiner, which was extensive. However, it does reference the evidence that was relied
upon with respect to forming forensic conclusions in this case. Additional material and
specific references / documents are also cited within the body of this report.




4 Access to justice is a basic right for all, and is solely the responsibility of the Government. The response

of the State to criminal complaints, or lack thereof, establishes the abilities and limitations set for the
complainant in this regard. In the State of Idaho, related rights are explicitly and implicitly detailed in the
Rights of Crime Victims (see Art. 1, sec. 22. of the State Constitution). The rights described within cannot
be secured without Due Diligence or Due Process. The United States Constitution also has a Due
Process requirement, which necessitates a thorough and competent investigation of all allegations
without deception or bias . These collective declarations establish that thorough and competent
investigations by the State are both a State and Federal right, which can only be satisfied by the due
diligence of government agents. Absent Due Diligence by state investigators, which is necessary for Due
Process, individual rights may be ignored or directly even violated.
                                                                                           Brent E. Turvey, PhD
                                                                          CSA: Idaho vs. Bryan C. Kohberger

in police custody at the Moscow Police Department. This occurred with the help of, and
under the supervision of, members of the Moscow Police Department. Anne Taylor and

evidence viewing took place over the course of an entire day on December 12, 2024.
Photographs were taken of all items opened and examined, including the suspected
vehicle, available bloody clothing, bedding / bedframes, and mattresses. It also included
examination of various knives collected during the law enforcement investigation, and
the Ka-Bar Knife Sheath mentioned later in this report.
